equivalent:
The guard's predicate is an IDENTITY, not a heuristic: a union of routes that all start at `root` has `cores - 1` edges exactly when the routing is prefix-closed (`route(root, m)` is the prefix of `route(root, b)` at every intermediate `m`). Prefix-closure makes `parent(c)` — the core before `c` in `route(root, c)` — single-valued and total on `cores \ {root}`, so `edges <= cores - 1`; every core is on some route from the root, so the union is connected and `edges >= cores - 1`. It also forces every route to be simple, since a repeated core would give one prefix two lengths. So the guard fires if and only if some variant is not prefix-closed.

Two invariants cut the space the claim has to hold over. (1) `dests = every core` DOMINATES every subset: the union over a subset is a connected subgraph of the full union containing the root, so if the full union is a tree every sub-union is a subtree. The claim is therefore per `(fabric, root)`, not per `(fabric, root, dests)`. (2) Routing on both tori is TRANSLATION-INVARIANT — `ring_delta` and `tri_vector` depend only on `(bx - ax) mod cols` and `(by - ay) mod rows`, and `walk` starts from the source's own coordinates — so `route(a, b)` is `route(0, b - a)` shifted and root 0 exhausts every root. The claim is then per SHAPE.

Per variant. Crossbar: `route(a, b)` is `[a, b]`, and its only intermediates are its endpoints. Mesh2D: the displacement is `(bx - ax, by - ay)`, which is ADDITIVE, so it commutes with truncation exactly, and `walk` emits all of x then all of y in unit steps. Torus2D: `ring_delta` returns `fwd` when `2*fwd <= n` and `fwd - n` otherwise, and it commutes with truncation by two inequalities. A FORWARD delta has `0 <= d` and `2d <= n`, so a prefix of `k <= d` has `2k <= n` and is chosen forward, equal to `k`. A BACKWARD delta has `2*fwd > n`, hence `|d| = n - fwd < n/2` STRICTLY, so a prefix at distance `k <= |d|` has `2k < n`, its own forward candidate `n - k` fails `2(n-k) <= n`, and it is chosen backward, equal to `-k`. The exact tie `2k == n` is the only value that could flip a prefix's direction, and the strict inequality on the backward branch is what makes it unreachable. TriangularTorus: the chosen representative `(x, y)` can never have both `2|x| > cols` and `2|y| > rows`, because the all-flipped representative `(x - cols*sgn(x), y - rows*sgn(y))` keeps the sign class and so has `tri_dist` equal to `max(cols-|x|, rows-|y|)` or `(cols-|x|) + (rows-|y|)` by that class, each strictly below `(x, y)`'s own — it would have won the key. With that bound `walk`'s prefixes are of only two shapes, `(j*sgn(x), j*sgn(y))` for `j <= min(|x|, |y|)` along the diagonal and then one coordinate at its full value while the other grows, which is the residual the five-level tie-break has to agree with.

What is MEASURED rather than derived is that last step for the triangular torus. Transcribing no model and calling the crate itself: 3,460,232 routes, every one checked for `route(root, m) == route(root, b)[..=i]` at EVERY intermediate — all four variants at every root of every shape to 12x12, both tori at root 0 for every shape to 40x40 plus 1,2,3,4,5,63,64,65,100,101,128,200 against 1,2,3,63,64,100,128,200, and crossbars to 40 cores at every root — zero violations and zero guard firings. This review did not locate an input on which the guard fires.

⛔ It did locate one before the fix in this file's `Fabric::cores_are_addressable`: past `u32::MAX + 1` cores, `walk` built each core's name as `row * cols + col` cast to a `u32` and the cast wrapped, so `multicast_tree(&Mesh2D { cols: 100_000, rows: 100_000 }, 4_294_967_295, &[5, 99_999])` returned `RouteUnionIsNotATree` with 185,892 cores over 185,892 links — the guard firing on a MESH because two of the routes it unioned named cores they never passed through. That is not a counterexample to prefix-closure; it is the reason `route`, `neighbours` and `multicast_tree` now refuse a fabric whose cores a `u32` cannot name, pinned by `a_fabric_with_cores_a_u32_cannot_name_is_refused_rather_than_truncated`. The guard's unreachability rests on that refusal as much as on the four variants.

equivalent: EQUIVALENT, by the symmetry of the structure the loop reads. `Adjacency::build` writes, for every synapse (pre, post) with pre != post, exactly one entry `post` into pre's block and exactly one entry `pre` into post's block, and it drops self-synapses at both ends. So the multiset of ordered pairs P = {(v, u) : u in adj.of(v)} is closed under swapping: (a, b) occurs in P exactly as many times as (b, a) does, namely once per synapse joining a and b in either direction (a reciprocal pair contributes one of each from each of its two synapses; two parallel synapses contribute two of each). The loop's whole effect is one increment per element of P. The old line's increment for the element (v, u) lands in cnt[v * k + core_of[u]]; the new line's increment for the SAME element lands in cnt[u * k + core_of[v]], which is precisely the cell the old line's increment for the element (u, v) lands in. Swapping is a bijection of P onto itself, so the two loops deposit the same number of increments into every cell, and the finished `cnt` array is identical element for element - for every network, every assignment and every core count, including multigraphs, reciprocal pairs and networks with self-synapses. Neither form can panic where the other does not: u and v are both below net.n and both core_of[u] and core_of[v] are below k, so both index expressions are in range for the same allocation. Nothing downstream reads the order of the increments, only the array they build, and the array does not differ. No test could tell, because there is nothing to tell: the only way to separate the two lines would be an adjacency whose pair multiset is NOT symmetric, and `Adjacency::build` is the only constructor there is.

equivalent: Every exchange in `applied` locks both of its neurons and the boundary set excludes locked neurons, so the pairs are pairwise disjoint in neurons. `kl_exchange` reads and writes only `core_of[u]`, `core_of[v]`, the `cnt` rows of u's and v's neighbours at columns cu and cv, and `syn[cu]`, `syn[cv]` — all derived from `core_of[u]` and `core_of[v]` alone, never from a neighbour's current core. Two undo operations on disjoint neuron pairs therefore commute: the `cnt` updates are additions of the same +-1 deltas whichever order they land in, and the `syn` updates are additions of the same in-degree differences. The state after undoing the tail is identical in either direction.
